originalTitle: Private ancestry packing across any number of fresh hosts
originalStatement: An old-value return x to the right of j fresh hosts has j distinct earlier private source rows, whose distinct diagonals lie in (x,T]. Therefore j≤T−x. Fresh hosts occur in increasing value order but need not be a physical suffix.
originalHypotheses: Canonical table, P02/P03/P05/P14/P16 and exact journal identity. No K2 or NoTriple assumption.
independence: Proof reconstructed from primary arguments and explicit definitions. Earlier source status/review assertions were not treated as proof. The author previously collected these sources; the present derivations and finite/exact-algebra checks are new independent audit work.
detailedDerivation: At a record row, earlier fresh outputs exceedT≥q. For a later returning valuex≤T, MEX inversion placesx in each earlier fresh host’s journal.

It is not an inherited seed: a diagonal owner left of a fresh host is also left of the current return host and seed exclusion forbids that current occurrence. A source at the fresh host’s birth is likewise forbidden by seed exclusion.
Thus every one ofj fresh hosts supplies a private source row c<a_c<q with valuex. Its source diagonal is strictly above x by row maximality and injectivity.
Two hosts cannot share a source row, or that row would repeatx. Their diagonal values are also distinct, all lying in(x,T], so j≤#{a<q:d(a)>x}≤T−x.

Fresh hosts themselves are in increasing value order: a later smaller fresh output would have to be in an earlier journal, contradicting journal ceilingT. This does not make the hosts a physical suffix, and the returning cell need not be live.
